title: Definite unitary groups and iterated theta lifts
summary: Over the host CM field the chapter fixes totally definite Hermitian spaces $X_0\subset X_1\subset\cdots\subset X_m$ of ranks $k+j(t+1)$, with $k\approx x^{9/2}$ and $m\approx\sqrt x$, indefinite companions $Y_j$, and Harish-Chandra parameters that interlace in the sense of Gan-Gross-Prasad. An algebraic modular form on $U(X_0)$ is lifted $m$ times by explicit theta kernels on classes of lattices, which realizes $\pi\mapsto\pi\boxplus\mu_1[t+1]\boxplus\cdots\boxplus\mu_m[t+1]$ for tuples $\mu$ of Hecke characters. The Rallis inner product formula shows that the first lifts do not vanish, a seesaw carries nonvanishing of periods up the tower, and the period of the iterated lift is identified, up to a nonzero constant, with a standard Bessel period.
progress: Fix pass: the flat map and the unfolding functional integrate over all of U_rho(A_E); Lemma th-first-lift-unique has the Lean's hypotheses; the proof of th-first-lift-comparison follows the Lean's steps, with the shorter argument as Remark th-first-lift-comparison-short; the mixed-model formulas are proved to the depth floor through the new Lemma th-mixed-origin, with Remark th-mixed-model-literature.

statements.statement: Ranks are integers $k,m,t$ and $n$ with $k$ and $m$ even, $t$ odd, $2\le m$, $m+3\le k$, $k+m+4\le t$, $3m<t$, $m\le2n\le k$ and $m^2\le k+m(t+1)$; put $f=2n$ and $N(j)=k+j(t+1)$. A rank datum also contains a Galois datum (hf-frame) whose group has order $n$. Here $n$ is the order of the $2$-power part of the Galois group of the host field, $f$ the number of complex embeddings used, $m$ the number of lifts, $t+1$ the rank added by each lift, and $k$ the rank of the first definite space.
statements.label: th-ranks

statements.statement: Let ranks be given. A Harish-Chandra parameter consists of $u\in(\tfrac12+\mathbf Z)^{k}$, $v\in\mathbf Z^{k-1}$ and $b,e\in\mathbf Z^{m}$ with $u_1>v_1>u_2>\cdots>v_{k-1}>u_k$, $-b_1<u_k$, $e_j-b_j\ge(t+3)/2$ for all $j$ and $b_{j+1}-e_j\ge(t+3)/2$ for $j<m$. (The weights on $U(X_j)$, $u$ followed by $j$ constant blocks of length $t+1$, are part of the definite-side datum.)
statements.label: th-hc-parameter

statements.statement: Hermitian spaces over $E/F$ with basis, signature and unimodular lattice; a system of spaces: definite $X_j$ of rank $N(j)$, $X'\subset X_m$ of corank one with an anisotropic orthogonal vector, $Y_j$ of rank $r+jt$ containing $X_j$ ($j<m$), $Y_0=X_0\oplus\langle z_0\rangle\oplus H^{r_S}$ with $h(z_0,z_0)=-T$, $W_j$ of rank $r$ locally isometric to $Y_0$, $V_j$ of rank $r+t$ with orthonormal lattice.
statements.label: th-spaces

statements.statement: A column chain: finite sets of classes with finite stabilizers, frame sets $Y_i$ with nonvanishing functions $\delta_i$, unit twists $\rho_i,\rho'_i$, arbitrary linear kernels $\vartheta_i(c,c')$, and exponents $s_i=e_{i+1}-N(i+1)/2$, $s'_i=e_{i+1}-N(i)/2$.
statements.label: th-column-chain

statements.statement: Let a chain of finite sets of lattice classes $\mathrm{cls}_0,\dots,\mathrm{cls}_m$ in the definite spaces $X_0,\dots,X_m$ be given, with finite stabilizers, determinant twists $\rho,\rho'$ and theta kernels $\theta(L,L')$ for $L\in\mathrm{cls}_i$, $L'\in\mathrm{cls}_{i+1}$. The $i$-th lift sends a vector-valued function $\varphi$ on $\mathrm{cls}_i$ to $K_i\varphi(L')=\sum_{L\in\mathrm{cls}_i}|\mathrm{Stab}\,L|^{-1}\rho(L)\rho'(L')\,\big(\Delta_{i}^{-1}\circ\theta(L,L')\circ\sharp_i\big)\varphi(L)$, where $\sharp_i$ and $\Delta_i$ multiply by fixed powers of the coordinate functions. The iterated lift is $K_{m-1}\circ\cdots\circ K_0$, a map from algebraic modular forms on $U(X_0)$ to algebraic modular forms on $U(X_m)$.
statements.label: th-iterated-lift

statements.statement: A definite-side datum consists of: ranks; a host CM field $E/F$ with auxiliary and level primes; a system of spaces $X_j$ (definite, rank $N(j)$), $X'\subset X_m$, $Y_j$, $W_j$, $V_j$; parameters $\lambda(\tau)$ for a set $\mathcal T$ of $f$ embeddings and per-word parameters labelled injectively by binary words of length $k-2$; for each word a column chain, data at an auxiliary prime $T_u=\pi\bar\pi$ with $\pi\equiv1$ and $T^*_u\le T_u\le(1+1/(fk))T^*_u$, and a period map; a Galois totally complex coefficient field $L$ with spaces of top forms and of forms, periods of the iterated lifts and Bessel pairings; determinant twists $\rho,\rho'$; lattices of forms with weights $u$ followed by constant blocks; Bessel-period data; and further data used in later chapters.
statements.label: th-definite-datum

statements.statement: The twisting data of a definite-side datum (fields ntw and nexp): twisting indices with primes and coefficient rings, ray class groups with Artin maps, signatures with Galois representations and Hecke eigenvalues, theta values, spaces of forms with theta data; the space V_0, theta lattices and twisted theta lattices, good signatures, Bloch-Kato lengths, the bound nu_i and twisted theta values, as used by the twist condition of Chapter 13.
statements.label: th-twisting-data

statements.statement: Remark: the kernels of the datum are abstract; where integrality is proved, each is required to be a constant-coefficient differential operator at the origin applied to a combination of translates of a theta function of the lattice pair $L+\bar\pi L^\vee$.
statements.label: th-lift-kernels

statements.statement: Theta functions on $\mathbb W=M(\mathbf A_E)$ quasi-periodic under rational points; Weil data with characters $(\chi_S,\chi_T)$ given by axioms (Heisenberg equivariance, automorphy at $0$, unitarity, splitting at split places); theta kernel $\omega(g,h)f(0)$ and theta lifts.
statements.label: th-weil-datum

statements.statement: Level systems (tuples $\mu_{t,j}=\mu^0_j\xi_t$) and theta grids: spaces $V_{i,j}$ of rank $r+jt+i(r+6)$ with $V_{0,j}=Y_j$, core spaces $P_i$, definite top spaces $Q_j$, embeddings, characters $\chi_i$, and Weil data on all grid pairs.
statements.label: th-grid

statements.statement: Bottom triples $(A,A',W)$ with identity Gram matrices and ranks $a(i,j),a'(i,j),a+a'$, Weil data with characters built from $\alpha_t,\beta$, standard theta functions at the ramified places, and the theta integrals $I_t,I'_t$ of $1$.
statements.label: th-bottom-triple

statements.statement: Partial Hecke $L$-functions (entire, Euler product over unramified places) and the quantifier 'for all sufficiently large data'.
statements.label: th-large-data

statements.reference: Rallis, Injectivity properties of liftings associated to Weil representations, Compositio Math. 52 (1984); Rallis, L-functions and the oscillator representation, LNM 1245 (1987); Harris-Kudla-Sweet, JAMS 9 (1996); Yamana, Invent. Math. 196 (2014); Gan-Qiu-Takeda, Invent. Math. 198 (2014)
statements.statement:
Assume the local theta inputs of Chapter 12. For all sufficiently large data, every grid Weil datum, all $0\le i,j<m$, every bottom triple $(A,A',W)$ of totally definite spaces with identity Gram matrices and ranks $a,a'$, $a+a'$, and every tuple $t$, there are a Fock polynomial $P$, a Haar measure $
u$, a fundamental domain $\mathcal F$ and $c
e0$ such that $\int_{\mathcal F}|I_t(P,h)|^2\,d
u(h)=c\prod_{s=1-e_0}^{h_0}\Lambda(s)$ for every entire $\Lambda$ equal to the partial Euler product of $
u_{t,i,j}$ (unramified places, no Gamma factors) for $\operatorname{Re}s>1$; here $I_t(P,\cdot)$ is the theta lift of $1$ from $U(A)$ to $U(W)$ and $e_0=(a-a')/2$, $h_0=(a+a')/2$.
statements.label: th-rallis-inner-product

statements.statement: The agreement of global and local theta integrals (convergence, a unique nonzero proportionality constant for matched vectors, its change along Witt towers) and the local matching; both proved from the Siegel-Weil literature.
statements.label: th-theta-hypotheses

statements.reference: Rallis, Compositio Math. 52 (1984); Kudla-Rallis, Ann. of Math. 140 (1994)
statements.statement: Assume the local theta inputs, the agreement of global and local theta integrals, the local matching of Chapter 12, and the nonvanishing of the relevant Hecke $L$-values. Then for all sufficiently large definite-side data, every Weil datum, every bottom triple and every $t$, both theta integrals of the triple are nonzero for some Schwartz function and some point.
statements.label: th-first-lift-nonzero

statements.statement: Tensor rules for orthogonal decompositions of either space of a pair: products and slices of theta functions are theta functions, and Weil data act factor by factor (proved for Weil data given by axioms).
statements.label: th-tensor-rule

statements.statement: For lines L, L' and tau: L' -> L multiplying the form by +-xi_0 xi_0bar, the map w -> (tau w)^* identifies theta functions for (L,S) and (S,L') (with complex conjugation for the sign +1) and intertwines the Weil data; every theta function for (S,L') arises this way.
statements.label: th-line-comparison

statements.statement: Let $D$ be a definite-side datum, and let $V_0=A\oplus L$ and $X=T\oplus L''$ be orthogonal decompositions of Hermitian spaces with $L,L''$ of rank one and $L''$ identified with a rescaling of $L$ by $-\xi_0\bar\xi_0$. For compatible Weil data on the pairs $(V_0,S)$, $(A,S)$, $(L,S)$, $(S,X)$, $(S,T)$ and $(S,L'')$ and theta functions $\Xi$ on $(V_0,S)$ and $\Phi_2$ on $(S,T)$, the products of Weil-representation actions on the two sides of the seesaw agree pointwise; in particular the corresponding theta kernels coincide.
statements.label: th-seesaw-identity

statements.statement: Matrix coefficients of theta functions: continuous and bounded, supported near a lattice in the finite directions, rapidly decreasing in the archimedean directions; their sums over rational translates are uniformly bounded.
statements.label: th-matrix-coefficients

statements.statement: Moyal orthogonality for theta functions; <f,f> != 0 for f != 0; translates of lattice vacua by the annihilator are lattice vacua, and other translates are orthogonal to all lattice vacua.
statements.label: th-lattice-vacua

statements.statement: A tame functional vanishing on the annihilator translates of a nonzero lattice vacuum vanishes on all lattice vacua.
statements.label: th-vacuum-irreducibility

statements.statement: For a Hermitian space $V$ and $g\in U(V)(\mathbf A)$: the height $\operatorname{ht}_0(g)=\prod_v\max(1,\|g\|_v,\|g^{-1}\|_v)$, the height on the quotient $\operatorname{ht}(g)=\inf_\gamma\operatorname{ht}_0(\gamma g)$, the archimedean size $\|a\|_\infty$, and the adelic size of a vector seen from $g$.
statements.label: th-heights

statements.statement: Polynomial growth of $(\omega(xa,yb)f)(w)$ in $(1+\|a\|_\infty)(1+\|b\|_\infty)$ for $a,b$ of finite component $1$, through the oscillator representation in the Fock model.
statements.label: th-archimedean-growth

statements.statement:
An $(N,B)$-sized subgroup $\Lambda$ of a Hermitian space over a CM field for a size function $
u$: stable under the integers, integral form, $N$ times the dual inside $\Lambda$, $
u$ subadditive with $
u(ax)\leq\operatorname{house}(a)
u(x)$ and $\operatorname{house}h(x,y)\leq
u(x)
u(y)$, $B\geq2$, and spanned by vectors with $
u\leq B$.
statements.label: th-sized-lattice

statements.statement: An $(N,B)$-sized lattice of rank $n$ contains an orthogonal basis with nonzero norms and sizes at most $B^k$, $k$ depending on $n$.
statements.label: th-anisotropic-frame

statements.statement: An $(N,B)$-sized lattice of rank $n\geq1$ contains a nonzero vector whose norm has house at most $C$ and whose size is at most $B^k$, by Minkowski's linear forms theorem on the trace form.
statements.label: th-short-vector

statements.statement: An $(N,B)$-sized lattice of rank $n\geq1$ contains a vector of size at most $B^k$ whose norm lies in a finite set $S\subset E^\times$ depending on $n$ and $N$.
statements.label: th-anisotropic-vector

statements.statement: An $(N,B)$-sized lattice of rank $n$ contains an orthogonal basis with norms in a finite set $S_0\subset E^\times$ and sizes at most $B^k$.
statements.label: th-orthogonal-frame

statements.statement: Reduction: every $g$ has $\gamma g=xak$ with $\gamma$ rational, $x$ in a finite set, $a$ archimedean with $1+\|a\|_\infty\leq C\operatorname{ht}_0(g)^M$ and $k$ in a given open subgroup.
statements.label: th-reduction

statements.statement: Mahler-type bound by sizes of rational vectors, a lower bound for those sizes, and two-sided comparisons of heights on the quotient along orthogonal sums and Witt decompositions.
statements.label: th-height-comparison

statements.statement: Estimates for Weil operators on theta functions: action on translations, joint continuity, polynomial growth in the heights, commutation with integrals of translates; comparison of heights along decompositions.
statements.label: th-weil-estimates

statements.statement: An integral of values of Weil operators against a weight decaying faster than any power of the heights is a tame map.
statements.label: th-kernel-tame

statements.statement: Let $D$ be a definite-side datum, $\iota_0\colon W_0\to W$ an isometry and $X=T\oplus L''$ with $L''$ of rank one, with compatible lattices $\Gamma,\Gamma_L,\Gamma_X$ and Weil data on $(W,T)$, $(W_0,X)$, $(W_0,-L'')$. Let $\varphi$ on $U(W_0)$ and $u$ on $U(T)$ be rapidly decreasing. If $\int_{[U(T)]}\theta_\Xi(\varphi)(h,1)u(h)\,dh\ne0$ for a lattice vacuum $\Xi$, then there are lattice vacua $\Phi,\Phi_0$ with $\int_{[U(W_0)]}\varphi(g)\theta_\Phi(u)(\iota_0g)\overline{\theta_{\omega_z}(g,1;\Phi_0)}\,dg\ne0$, the depth-zero Fourier-Jacobi period.
statements.label: th-seesaw-period-nonvanishing

statements.statement: Bessel and Fourier-Jacobi periods for $V=V_0\oplus H^\rho$, and the top Bessel period of the grid.
statements.label: th-periods

statements.statement: Row data and partial row lifts along $V_{0,0}=Y_0\to\cdots\to V_{m,0}$; column chains of core forms on $U(P_i)$, each the theta lift of the next.
statements.label: th-core-chain

statements.statement: Hyperbolic decompositions, Bessel data, Fourier-Jacobi data, steps between them (Weil data for the pair and for the anisotropic parts), and the flat map built from the mixed model.
statements.label: th-step

statements.statement: Local data (S, Gamma_0, K) for a step: theta functions stable under real and annihilator translations, flat maps lattice vacua, K-invariance, support condition, nonvanishing.
statements.label: th-step-local

statements.statement: The Fourier-Jacobi functional of all data l_{phi,G}(Xi) and the handed-down function phi_Xi.
statements.label: th-step-periods

statements.statement: The period functionals are tame; product formulas for l_{phi,G}(Xi_1 x Xi_2) and phi_{Xi_1 x Phi'}; the flat map commutes with Heisenberg translations.
statements.label: th-step-functionals

statements.statement: The mixed model $f_x$ of a theta function along a hyperbolic decomposition: Heisenberg laws, Fourier expansion over rational $x$, and the formulas for the target group, the core group, the Levi factor and the unipotent radical.
statements.label: th-mixed-model

statements.statement: Unfolding: the integral over the flag group of a theta lift against a weight with the character and transvection conditions equals the integral over a fundamental domain of U(W)(F) cap R_{x_0} of G times the flat-map functional.
statements.label: th-unfolding

statements.statement: For a step from Bessel to Fourier-Jacobi data: the base point has Gram matrix $0$ and $R_{x_0}$ is the Jacobi group; the conjugate Bessel character satisfies the conditions of the unfolding lemma; and $\ell_\Theta(\Psi)=\Psi^\flat(0)$.
statements.label: th-bessel-unfolding

statements.statement: Fourier uniqueness on the archimedean coordinates of the base points, and the description of strips $R(\mathbf A)CU(W)(\mathbf A)_f$ by a measurable set read on archimedean components.
statements.label: th-fourier-strips

statements.statement: If the Bessel (resp. Fourier-Jacobi) period of the lift vanishes for all theta functions of the local data, the auxiliary functional vanishes at their flat maps (unfolding).
statements.label: th-vanishing-descends

statements.statement: One step of the tower: a nonzero Fourier-Jacobi period of a lift gives a nonzero Bessel period of a lift on the next space, and conversely.
statements.label: th-step-nonvanishing

statements.statement: Complex conjugation turns the grid Weil data of the row and core pairs into Weil data with inverse characters, and the column chain and partial row lifts into theta lifts; the partial row lift at i depends only on row data below i.
statements.label: th-grid-conjugation

statements.statement: For the lattice $\Lambda$ of a pair of self-dual lattices: $\Lambda$ is its own annihilator, and each $u\in\Lambda$ acts on all lattice vacua for $\Lambda$ by one sign.
statements.label: th-lattice-signs

statements.statement: Coset vectors are nonzero Fock vacua and lattice vacua for the depth lattice; translations by finite elements of the annihilator move a conjugate coset vector to a multiple of another.
statements.label: th-coset-vectors

statements.statement: At a split place, for a subgroup $\Lambda$ whose $\bar e$-half detects the $e$-half outside $\Lambda$ and a nonzero $f$ fixed by $\Lambda$ in both halves: a linear form $\kappa$ with $\kappa(f)=1$ and $\kappa(\rho(y)f)\geq0$ on the $e$-half, and a linear form $\ell$ with $\ell(f)\neq0$ invariant under the $e$-half on theta functions.
statements.label: th-invariant-form

statements.statement: At a split place, a theta function killed by all functionals invariant under one half, after translations by the other half, is zero.
statements.label: th-split-separation

statements.statement: At a nonsplit place where the characters are unramified, the lattice stabilizers fix theta functions invariant under the local lattice translations.
statements.label: th-nonsplit-vacua

statements.statement: Depth-type theta functions of the row and core pairs are fixed by the congruence subgroups; row data are of depth type; partial row lifts are right invariant under the congruence subgroups.
statements.label: th-depth-fixed

statements.statement: A tame map vanishing on the polynomials in the creation operators applied to a Fock vacuum vector vanishes on its archimedean translates.
statements.label: th-fock-translates

statements.statement: A tame functional vanishing on the conjugated Fock vectors of all coset vectors vanishes on all lattice vacua of the row depth lattice.
statements.label: th-fock-span

statements.statement: Tower decompositions of the grid (Lean: Frames), fitting the ends, and good for line lattices Gamma_L.
statements.label: th-tower-decomposition

statements.statement: The standard tower decomposition built from the bases of the complements of the core spaces, scaled by powers of -xi_0, fits the ends and is good for explicit line lattices.
statements.label: th-standard-tower

statements.statement: Tower decompositions that fit the ends and are good exist; (J_0) follows from the base period; (J_k) implies (B_k); (B_k) implies (J_{k+1}).
statements.label: th-tower-rungs

statements.statement: For every definite-side datum with $p_{de},p'_{de}$ prime to $Q_Sq$, every theta grid with Weil data, every column chain $\Psi_0,\dots,\Psi_m$ of core forms (each the theta lift of the next) and every $u$ on $U(Y_0)$ with rapidly decreasing row lifts: if $\int\Psi_0(\iota_0h)u(h)\,dh\ne0$, then the top Bessel period of $\Psi_m$ against the $m$-fold row lift $\theta^{(m)}(u)$ is nonzero for some row data. The hypothesis on depth data is proved, so the statement is unconditional.
statements.label: th-bessel-ascent

statements.statement: Let $D$ be a definite-side datum. The Bessel identity for $D$ holds if the Bessel pairings of $D$ are rational and there is an isometry $V$ of the space of top forms such that for every word $u$ there are $a_u\ne0$ and an isometry $U_u$ with $B_u(\varphi,F)=a_u\,\mathcal B_u(U_u\varphi,VF)$ for all $\varphi,F$, where $\mathcal B_u$ is the standard Bessel period. It is part of the division link of Chapter 8, where it identifies the period of the iterated lift with a Bessel period that does not depend on the tuple of Hecke characters.
statements.label: th-bessel-identity
